obligations.note: The catalog fixes auto-approval at 40% DTI and 90% LTV, but head sets Policy.DTI_MAX_PERCENT and mortgage.dti_max_percent to 43, so cases between 40% and 43% DTI can auto-approve. The renewed proof still assumes DTI_MAX_PERCENT = 40, and no CRD-1 exception covers the change.

Ticket CHG-25598 is approved by change manager Erik Brandt before review, and its components (mortgage.policy, mortgage.tests, mortgage.controls-data) cover Policy.java, UnderwritingTest.java, and controls/mortgage/policy-params.json.
Wen Li, a baseline-mortgage change approver and not the author Declan Farrell, approved a code review of the head commit.
The change is a single commit, and both the code review and the control-owner approval name 841b40711faf3ac9834648a72a43f5d51fcc440a.

records/ci/run.json records a successful baseline-mortgage suite on the head commit, and the JUnit report shows 124 tests with no failures, errors, or skips, including controls.UnderwritingControlTest#autoApproveGridMatchesPolicy.
The touched components mortgage.policy, mortgage.tests, and mortgage.controls-data are not security_sensitive, so a security review is not required.

policy-params.json is a protected controls path and an approved policy value. Bao Tran, a control owner on the controls-office team rather than the author's lending-eng team, approved the head commit.
CHG-25598 is a standard ticket and the change is not emergency, so a post-implementation review is not due.

Moving the DTI ceiling off the approved 40% is a CRD-1 deviation with no approved, unexpired exception scoped to that obligation. EXC-0141 expired on 2026-09-12, EXC-0167 is LOG-1, and EXC-0172 is withdrawn.

Ledger entry ACR-0406 covers Policy.DTI_MAX_PERCENT, and this change alters that constant from 40 to 43, so the prior proof lapses. The replacement proof names the head commit but still premises DTI_MAX_PERCENT = 40, so it is not valid evidence for the merged code.

summary: Process records for the ticket, independent code review, control-owner approval, and the mortgage test run are in order, and the edit does not touch a security-sensitive component or an emergency path. The product change still raises the auto-approve DTI ceiling from the catalog's approved 40% to 43% in both Policy.java and policy-params.json. That violates CRD-1. No qualifying exception covers it, and the renewed proof still assumes a 40% ceiling, so the lapsed CRD-1 evidence is not replaced. The change cannot be accepted.
